geometry_edits.rationale: Add a courtyard macro so the existing mass becomes a clearer neighborhood-building figure with an active ground void.
Increase carve depth to make the court legible in plan and section.
Orient the opening toward the verified frontage/access side.
Make the new courtyard-bearing macro the root so the public void governs the compiled mass.

graph_edits.rationale: Transform the protected ground-edge notch into a more legible public court while keeping the compact bar ancestry.
Deepen the carved open space so it reads as usable public void rather than a minor chip.
Align the void with the verified access side in the program frame to strengthen the public threshold.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent compact bar with a single dominant gesture, and the top/front/opposite views broadly agree. The notch at one end creates some ground-level articulation, but the public void is shallow and not yet legible enough as a usable courtyard/cut in the neighborhood-living sense. The mass is also somewhat box-like and the section remains nearly flat, so it lacks the stronger public threshold and inhabited section logic seen in the references. It is not visually broken or self-colliding, so repair integrity is decent, but program appropriateness is only partial because the active edge and public-space contract are underexpressed. The form could support neighborhood living if the access edge were opened more decisively with a deeper carve or courtyard while preserving the dominant compact mass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More sculptural and pavilion-like than a compact neighborhood living block; roof articulation is stronger than this candidate’s current section logic.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise massing with a carved central void and a bridge-like upper connection to keep the ground active.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Sports-mall ring typology is not directly analogous to a neighborhood living mass; do not copy the circular plan.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A sunken/open center and perimeter mass can create a public interior while preserving a clear outer envelope.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Too dispersed and large-scale to transplant directly; candidate is much more compact and should remain so.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like clustering around a central court can support mixed-use hierarchy and public space.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Facade transparency is not the point; the massing move is the carve/void and threshold condition.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A rectangular block gains program fit through a large cutout and overhang that activate the street edge.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is more linear and site-spread than the candidate; avoid overextending the footprint.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: An elongated low-rise mass with a central atrium and folded/sloping roof can reconcile public interior space with calm upper massing.

warnings: Parcel boundary is present and the mass appears contained, but it should respond more clearly to the parcel rather than simply occupying it.
The verified access edge is read as the blue frontage; current response is too sealed/opposite and needs a more legible public threshold.
Program fit fails the hard gate because the visible section/void logic is too weak for the required neighborhood_living public edge and active ground condition.
